title: Unit Cost Lens: Pricing Journey Mapper for Console Exports
creator: Rosa Chen
description: Design and prototype a horizontally navigable "unit cost lens" in the Redwood Console that maps token-level usage to pricing slabs, attribution groups, and exportable CSV/JSON for finance and product teams. This ticket covers the interaction model, two export formats (line-item and aggregated), and a compact pricing overlay to preview bill impact for alternate pricing slabs.
background: Customers ask for transparency at the token and request level to reconcile invoices and debug anomalies. Current cost views are either too aggregated (per-route) or too noisy (raw logs). We need a middle-ground UI that surfaces per-token breakout, attribution to prompts/flows, and an export path compatible with chargeback and forecasting workflows.
user_stories: As a finance analyst, I want to download a line-item CSV showing tokens, model, prompt id, user id, and price per token so I can reconcile monthly bills.
As an engineer, I want to quickly filter requests by model and prompt to find costly outliers and link to the trace in observability.
As a product manager, I want to simulate switching a route to a different pricing slab and see projected monthly savings.
As a platform operator, I want export templates that map to our existing chargeback system (account_id, cost_center, sku).
As a designer, I want a compact pricing overlay that explains slab math and rounding rules without leaving the lens.
As a privacy officer, I need the export to optionally redact PII before download.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive prototype in Figma showing token-level rows, aggregation controls, and pricing overlay
Two export formats implemented in the spec: line-item CSV and aggregated monthly rollup JSON
Filtering UX for model, route, prompt set, timeframe, and attribution tags
Mocked pricing simulation panel that projects monthly cost delta when switching slabs
Accessibility pass: keyboard navigation and screen-reader labeling for table and overlay
Design spec includes copy, edge-case handling for rate-limited tokens, and redaction toggle wording
design_notes: Prioritized a compact table view with inline expansion for full request payload to keep top-level density low. Use avatar+chip for attribution group (account/cost-center) and a tiny sparklines column to show per-request token split (prompt vs completion). Pricing overlay should surface base unit price, slab thresholds, any tiered discounts, and rounding rules. We will reuse console color tokens and the table components from the billing team.
decisions: Use line-item primary view with optional aggregation panel (rather than top-level aggregation by default) to balance discoverability and performance
Exports will support both CSV (finance-friendly) and JSON (platform integrations) with a standard header mapping to existing chargeback keys
Pricing simulation will operate on a sampling window (default 7 days) and extrapolate to monthly for projection to keep compute cheap for large accounts
PII redaction implemented client-side as an export option (toggle) in the UI spec rather than server-side for the initial release
open_questions: Which exact set of fields does Finance need in the canonical export? (requested: account_id, cost_center, route_id, prompt_id, user_id, model, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, unit_price, cost_usd, timestamp)
Should pricing simulation allow custom slabs defined by enterprise customers or only pick from configured plans?
How should we surface refunds or credits tied to specific token lines in the export?
What's the expected max row count for exports before we require async generation?

implementation_notes: Prototype will use a server-sampled dataset for the simulation and mock exports. Engineering to propose an API with pagination and export job endpoint. Use existing billing SKU mapping as single source of truth. Track export generation time and file size for telemetry and potential rate limits.
risks_and_mitigations: Large exports may time out: mitigate with async exports and chunking
Misaligned export fields with Finance needs: mitigate by running a field sign-off and delivering a sample CSV early
PII leakage risk: mitigate with explicit redaction toggle and preserve audit log of export requests
